name: ZenCommunity — Real-Time Community with Messaging, Feeds, Live Chat & Support System
author: Kodezen LLC

sections.description:
The All-in-One WordPress Community Plugin for Groups, Social Feeds, Real-Time Chat, and Support

ZenCommunity is the first WordPress community plugin that unifies groups, posts, support ticketing, and live chat into one native powerhouse. Build social, Facebook-style communities with real-time chat and posts, convert community posts into tracked support tickets, and offer instant live help — all inside your WordPress site.

👉 ZenCommunity Site
👉 Unlock Premium Features
👉 Join Our Official Community

Core Features at a Glance

Community Tool

  • User-friendly UX
  • Unlimited groups/spaces
  • User profiles
  • Activity feeds
  • Member controls
  • Feeds
  • Comments & reactions
  • Real-time chat
  • Notifications
  • Privacy controls
  • Mentions
  • Hashtags
  • Polls and surveys (Coming soon)
  • Leaderboard (Coming soon)
  • Bookmarks
  • Branding options
  • Welcome message
  • Custom slugs
  • Search
  • Member directory
  • File uploads
  • GIF
  • Emoji
  • Media storage
  • Role manager
  • User approval
  • Email summaries
  • Dark & light mode

Support Ticketing [PRO]

  • Convert feed to tickets
  • Ticket status tracking
  • Ticket assignment
  • Ticket stages (ongoing, solved, etc.)
  • Ticket notifications
  • Auto replies (Coming soon)

Live Chat [PRO]

  • Customizable website live chat widget (Cross domain also supported)
  • Multi-session handling
  • Instant visitor support
  • Real-time notifications
  • File sharing
  • 24/7 support system

ZenCommunity isn’t just another community plugin. It’s the first WordPress solution that combines the three strongest engagement systems — Community, Real-Time Chat, and Support Tickets — together in one place.

Most WordPress websites use 3–5 different tools to achieve what ZenCommunity does alone. That creates scattered conversations, missed messages, and poor user experience. ZenCommunity removes that problem completely.

By keeping community posts, chats, and support inside one system, your users stay connected, engaged, and supported without ever leaving your site.
Below are the core sections that show how ZenCommunity stands out.

Community Features — Your Full Social System Inside WordPress

ZenCommunity gives you everything needed to build a full, social-style community inside WordPress — no third-party platforms, no separate plugins.

Advanced Community Groups

Build public or private groups with full admin control. Groups can be used for LMS classes, client spaces, internal teams, membership circles, or interest-based communities. Each group has its own feed, members, and settings.

Facebook-Style Posting & Engagement

Your members can publish posts, attach media, use @mentions, comment, reply, react, and follow discussions. The interface feels familiar, simple, and fast — encouraging users to talk and stay active.

Real-Time Community Chat

ZenCommunity includes built-in chat inside groups. Members can start private one-to-one chats or chat as a group with typing indicators, read status, file sharing, and notifications. Conversations stay active without page reloads.

User Profiles & Activity Tracking

Each user gets a profile with activity, groups, posts, and engagement. This makes your community feel more personal and interactive.

Community Growth Features

Hashtags, polls, surveys, leaderboards, bookmarks, and email summaries help keep engagement high. Members always have a reason to come back.

Admin Control & Community Safety

Moderators can manage posts, approve members, customize branding, set privacy rules, and control roles. You decide how open or private each group should be.

Support Ticketing — Full Helpdesk Inside Your Community

ZenCommunity includes a complete support ticketing system connected directly to your community and chats.

Convert Posts Into Support Tickets

If a user posts a question that needs deeper help, convert it into a ticket with one click — no platform switching.

Clear Ticket Assignments

Assign each ticket to a responsible team member so the right person handles the issue. This reduces confusion and improves response time.

Status Tracking

Each ticket has clear stages (new, ongoing, solved, etc.) so both sides can follow progress. Your support team stays organized, and users always know what’s happening.

Personal Support Chat on Each Ticket

Tickets include an instant one-to-one chat. Users don’t need email or external help desks — everything is live and inside your site.

Smart Notifications

Both users and team members get notifications when ticket updates happen. Nothing gets lost.

Auto Replies

Helpful for off-hours, acknowledgment messages, or routing requests.

Live Chat — Instant Help That Converts Visitors

ZenCommunity includes a built-in real-time live chat widget for your entire site.

Customizable Widget

Add your supporter’s name, photo, availability status, and greeting message. This makes your support feel personal and trustworthy.

Instant Visitor Support

Visitors can start chatting immediately. Control visitor login or anonymous chat.

Multi-Session Handling

Support agents can handle multiple conversations at once without losing track.

Real-Time Notifications & File Sharing

Send and receive files instantly, get notified when new messages arrive, and keep the conversation going smoothly.

24/7 Support System

The widget stays active at all times, so users always have access to help.

Who ZenCommunity Helps

ZenCommunity fits a wide range of websites and business types:

  • LMS websites (students + instructors)
  • Membership sites
  • Local groups & communities
  • Agencies
  • SaaS companies
  • E-commerce stores
  • Service providers
  • Creators & educators
  • Internal teams & organizations

🔥 Deep Academy LMS Integration

ZenCommunity connects directly with Academy LMS to automate all your course activities inside your community — without any extra work from the admin.
When this integration is enabled, key Academy LMS events automatically create posts in your ZenCommunity groups. This means your learners stay updated, active, and informed without any manual posting.

What Automatically Gets Shared

ZenCommunity can post updates in your community when any of the following events happen inside Academy LMS:

  • Course Enrolled
  • Course Complete
  • Course Announcements
  • User Question
  • Question Answer
  • Lesson Update
  • Quiz Start
  • Quiz End

This makes ZenCommunity the perfect LMS community plugin.

Extended LMS Integrations

ZenCommunity now supports multiple popular WordPress LMS plugins, making it easy to add community, discussion, chat, and support features to your learning website.

Tutor LMS Integration with ZenCommunity

ZenCommunity integrates with Tutor LMS to bring key course activities directly into your community groups, helping learners stay informed and engaged inside WordPress.

This integration turns Tutor LMS course progress into visible community updates, encouraging discussion around learning milestones.

Tutor LMS Events Shared in ZenCommunity

When Tutor LMS integration is enabled, the following course activities are automatically posted in ZenCommunity group feeds:

  • Course Enrollment
  • Topic Complete
  • Course Complete
  • Quiz Start
  • Quiz End

Each event appears inside the selected community group, allowing students and instructors to interact around real course progress in real time.

LearnPress Integration with ZenCommunity

ZenCommunity integrates with LearnPress to connect course activity, learner questions, and progress updates directly with your community groups.

This integration helps LearnPress users turn learning actions into shared discussions, keeping students active and connected inside WordPress.

LearnPress Events Shared in ZenCommunity

When LearnPress integration is enabled, the following course activities are automatically posted in ZenCommunity group feeds:

  • Course Enrollment
  • Course Complete
  • Lesson Completion
  • User Question
  • Question Answer
  • Quiz Start
  • Quiz End

These updates appear inside the selected community groups, allowing learners and instructors to interact around real learning progress in one place.

MasterStudy LMS Integration with ZenCommunity

ZenCommunity integrates with MasterStudy LMS to connect course progress, learner questions, and completion updates directly with your community groups.

This integration helps MasterStudy-based learning sites turn course activity into shared discussions, keeping learners engaged inside WordPress.

MasterStudy LMS Events Shared in ZenCommunity

When MasterStudy LMS integration is enabled, the following course activities are automatically posted in ZenCommunity group feeds:

  • Course Enrollment
  • Course Complete
  • Lesson Completion
  • User Question
  • Question Answer
  • Quiz End

These updates appear inside the selected community groups, allowing students and instructors to interact around real learning progress in one place.

Lifter LMS Integration with ZenCommunity

ZenCommunity integrates with Lifter LMS to bring course activity, learner questions, and progress updates directly into your community groups.

This integration helps Lifter LMS websites keep students engaged through shared discussions and real-time updates inside WordPress.

Lifter LMS Events Shared in ZenCommunity

When Lifter LMS integration is enabled, the following course activities are automatically posted in ZenCommunity group feeds:

  • Course Enrollment
  • Course Complete
  • Lesson Completion
  • User Question
  • Question Answer
  • Quiz End

These updates appear inside the selected community groups, allowing learners and instructors to interact around real course progress in one central place.

LearnDash Integration with ZenCommunity

LearnDash integrates with ZenCommunity to connect course activity directly with your community groups, helping learners stay active and engaged inside WordPress.

This integration turns LearnDash progress into shared community updates, encouraging discussion, motivation, and peer interaction around learning milestones.

LearnDash Events Shared in ZenCommunity

When LearnDash integration is enabled, the following course activities are automatically posted in ZenCommunity group feeds:

  • Course Enrollment
  • Course Complete
  • Topic Complete
  • Quiz End

Each event appears inside the selected community group, allowing students and instructors to interact around real course progress in real time.

This makes ZenCommunity a strong companion for LearnDash-based learning sites that want to combine structured courses with active community engagement.

⚡ Performance & Reliability

  • ZenCommunity is built for speed:
  • No external tools
  • No outside servers
  • No extra apps
  • Everything loads inside WordPress
  • Real-time updates with lightweight scripts
    The plugin is optimized for both small sites and enterprise-level communities.

🛠 Admin Tools

Site admins get:

  • A single dashboard for groups, posts, tickets, and chats
  • Role-based permissions
  • Community moderation controls
  • Branding settings
  • Full visibility into engagement and support activity

Source Code

The compiled JavaScript and CSS in assets/build/ are generated from human-readable sources kept in the public repository:

https://github.com/kodezen/zencommunity

  • JavaScript/React sources: dev_zencommunity/ (admin app in dev_zencommunity/Admin/, block editor integration in dev_zencommunity/fse/)
  • Build configuration: package.json, webpack.config.js, tailwind.config.js, tailwind.admin.config.js, postcss.config.js
  • PHP dependencies: composer.json

To build the assets yourself:

  1. Clone the repository and install Node.js 20 or later and Composer.
  2. Run npm ci --legacy-peer-deps, then npm run build (compiles everything into assets/build/).
  3. Run composer install to install the PHP dependencies.

External services

ZenCommunity works entirely on your own site. It contacts an external service only in the cases below.

Kodezen usage insights and deactivation feedback (store.kodezen.com)

ZenCommunity uses the StoreEngine SDK to talk to Kodezen’s store at https://store.kodezen.com/.

  • Usage insights (opt-in only). After installation, an admin notice asks whether you want to share usage data. Nothing is sent unless an administrator clicks “Allow”. If you allow it, the plugin sends: site URL and name, admin name and email, server IP address, operating system, WordPress/PHP/MySQL and server versions, PHP settings and extensions, locale, multisite status, the active theme, active and inactive plugins, and the plugin version. After that it reports the same data about once a week. You can opt out at any time under ZenCommunity → Settings → License.
  • Deactivation feedback. When you deactivate the plugin, an optional form asks why and lists what will be sent. Only if you click “Submit & Deactivate” does it send the reason, any comment you type, your name and email, the site name and URL, and the usage data listed above. Choosing “Skip & Deactivate” sends nothing.

This service is provided by Kodezen: Terms of Use, Privacy Policy.

Link previews (the websites members link to)

When a logged-in member hovers over a link in a post or comment, your site fetches that link’s page once to show its title, description and image in a preview card. The request goes from your server to the linked website, and sends only the page address and a user agent that names your site. Nothing about the member is sent. For video and media links (for example YouTube or Vimeo) the details come from that service’s public oEmbed endpoint, from the list of providers built into WordPress, instead of the page itself. Results are cached for a day. The preview image is then loaded by the member’s browser from the linked website. Nothing is fetched until someone hovers over a link, and logged-out visitors see only the address. Developers can turn this off with add_filter( 'zencommunity/link_preview/enabled', '__return_false' );. Each linked website’s own terms and privacy policy apply.

Links to other Kodezen products

The “Extend your Community” dashboard section and the Live Chat settings link to product pages and downloads on https://store.kodezen.com/. These are plain links that open in your browser, and no data is sent until you click one. Products hosted on WordPress.org (for example GameEngine, GemBooking and Zaplane) are installed only when an administrator clicks “Install”. They come from WordPress.org through WordPress’s own plugin installer.
sections.faq:
Does ZenCommunity support real-time chat?

Yes. Both group and private chats are real-time.

Can I convert posts into support tickets?

Yes — any post or chat can become a ticket with one click.

Does it work with LMS platforms?

Yes, especially with Academy LMS where it integrates deeply.

Is live chat included?

A full live chat widget is included but it’s our Pro Features

Is this a complete WordPress community plugin?

Yes. It covers groups, posts, chat, and support — all together.
sections.changelog:
3.0.4 – 18/10/2026

  • Changed – Refreshed colors across the admin, frontend and setup wizard with new light and dark palettes. Sites still using the old default colors are updated automatically; custom colors are kept.
  • Changed – Community pages now use the active theme’s font instead of the bundled Inter font.
  • Changed – The admin submenu now uses WordPress’s standard menu styling.
  • Changed – Settings and Tools use a full-width layout with a collapsible, grouped side menu, and the settings content scrolls on its own.
  • Changed – Cards and panels use borders instead of shadows.
  • Changed – The new ticket form pre-selects the product, type, priority and assignee.
  • Changed – The “Ticket list” back link always opens the tickets page.
  • Changed – Guests can open the mobile and tablet menu, and the Follow button is hidden for guests and on your own member card.
  • Improved – Ticket sidebar: lighter selected card, bordered search field and easier-to-read status labels.
  • Improved – Primary buttons stay filled in dark mode, and the active menu item and role badges use the brand color in both modes.
  • Improved – Added accessible labels to the search, theme toggle, view switch and more-options buttons.
  • Improved – Clearer wording: a “Groups” heading, correct plural member counts, a “No more members” message and an empty state for Courses.
  • Fixed – The width of ticket cards in the ticket details sidebar.
  • Fixed – Column widths in the ticket table, and status labels that were hard to read in dark mode.
  • Fixed – The group hover card popup.
  • Fixed – Link colors and link previews in comments.

3.0.3 – 12/10/2026

  • Changed – The admin menu styles load only on ZenCommunity’s own screens, and the menu icon is now a 20×20 SVG that needs no CSS on other screens.
  • Changed – If the site’s PHP or WordPress version is below the minimum (PHP 7.4, WordPress 6.8), ZenCommunity no longer loads, and an admin notice explains why.
  • Changed – The setup wizard redirect after activation no longer interrupts WordPress’s activation process, so activating through the REST API, WP-CLI or bulk activation works normally.
  • Changed – Updated the StoreEngine SDK to 1.6.2 and Action Scheduler to 4.2.0.
  • Fixed – PHP 8.4 deprecation notices printed during activation and in admin screens.
  • Fixed – A PHP 7.4 parse error in the background process log.
  • Fixed – Database tables are now defined in the format dbDelta() requires, so updates no longer rebuild every column on each run.
  • Fixed – In-app-only notifications no longer write “Record not found.” entries to the debug log.
  • Fixed – The password reset, login and permalink settings links, and the REST API addresses used by the LMS course pickers, webhooks and live chat, now work with plain permalinks, custom login URLs and WordPress installed in a subdirectory.
  • Fixed – Missing translator comments for gamification messages.
  • Security – Theme color settings, admin notices, the admin menu script and error messages are now escaped when output.
  • Security – Uploaded SVG files are rejected when PHP’s DOM extension is unavailable, instead of being stored without checks.

3.0.2 – 11/10/2026

  • Changed – Reports & analytics and Audio/Video posts and Spaces now ship entirely in ZenCommunity Pro; the free plugin shows what they offer.
  • Changed – Poll posts and the Login & Registration settings are now available without Pro.
  • Changed – “Extend your Community” installs Kodezen products from WordPress.org only; products not on WordPress.org link to their product page.
  • Changed – The Inter font is bundled with the plugin instead of loading from Google Fonts.
  • Security – Registering with the email of an auto-created guest account now sends a confirmation link to that email instead of claiming the account immediately.
  • Security – Notification email links no longer sign the recipient in automatically.
  • Fixed – Uploaded files are located through the uploads directory, so sites with a custom content directory work.
  • Fixed – Some error messages used the wrong text domain.

3.0.1 – 10/10/2026

  • Fixed – A crash on the community’s error screen when ZCLabel was referenced without being imported, in the icon sidebar and ticket details drawer.
  • Fixed – Chat heads now dock and stack up to three can be open at once, each as its own fixed, non-draggable bubble/window pair with separate minimize and dismiss actions, instead of one draggable bubble that got replaced every time a new conversation opened.
  • Fixed – Several hard-coded, untranslatable strings flagged in a WordPress.org plugin review: “My Community” and the permalink/configuration admin notices, the “Feeds”/”Groups” navigation labels, relative timestamps (“X hr ago”) which now follow the site’s language, the “Public”/”Published” status badges in Spaces and Posts, and react-select’s “Select…”/”No options” defaults used throughout the community.
  • Fixed – Additional untranslated strings found by auditing the compiled build output: image preview loading/error text, audio recorder and ticket navigation labels, ticket date-filter placeholders, profile edit form placeholders, and feed post image alt text.

3.0.0 – 07/10/2026

  • Added – A guided Setup Wizard for new installs: environment checks, community details, a “what kind of community is this” type picker, and module toggles, ending in a launch summary. Re-run it anytime from the Dashboard’s “Re-run Setup Wizard” action.
  • Added – Two new Space types, Audio and Video (ZenCommunity Pro), that embed a watch-verified video or audio item configured in the TruePlayer plugin directly inside a community Space.
  • Added – A Reports page (ZenCommunity Pro) with Overview, Members, Spaces, Events, and Content tabs: trend charts, a leaderboard, a popular day/time heatmap, date-range filtering, and CSV export, plus a “last 7 days” summary on the Dashboard.
  • Added – Settings → User Management can now sync a member’s profile from their WordPress user account.
  • Added – Settings → AI Agent → Knowledge Base redesigned: “Generate from a Website” and “Keep it updated automatically” are now separate sub-tabs instead of stacked one below the other, and finishing a crawl surfaces its next-step actions (attach, upload, download, discard) in a clearly separated card instead of blending into the crawl progress area.
  • Added – Tools and Add-ons are now their own admin pages. Tools holds AI Agent, Migration and a shortcut to re-run the Setup Wizard; Add-ons gets search plus Status (All / Active / Inactive / Pro) and Category filters, and shows locked Pro add-ons with a PRO tag and an upgrade link when ZenCommunity Pro isn’t active.
  • Added – Setup Wizard: after picking a Space type you can set the Space’s name, slug, description, thumbnail, privacy and who can view its members before launching.
  • Added – Notifications dropdown filters: All, Unread and Read, each loaded from the server.
  • Added – A fullscreen image viewer for post photos, with previous/next, keyboard navigation, thumbnails and download.
  • Added – A new emoji picker with search, categories and recently used emojis in the post composer, edit and anonymous post forms, Chat, chat-head windows, message reactions and Live Chat.
  • Improved – Redesigned the Dashboard, left sidebar, top navigation, Spaces table, and the Add Space/Add Collection/New Post forms for a cleaner, more professional admin panel.
  • Improved – Refreshed the support ticket, live chat, and community feed screens’ UI.
  • Improved – Updated StoreEngine’s licensing SDK to 1.5.9: no more license-server calls on every admin page load, batched background update checks, and a circuit breaker that stops retrying while the license server is down.
  • Improved – The ZenCommunity admin menu is more compact: Spaces, Posts, Users and Collections are grouped under a “Community” flyout (and dropdown in the top bar), with dividers between sections and Add-ons highlighted.
  • Improved – Admin forms use notched field labels throughout, with searchable dropdowns and brand-coloured checkboxes.
  • Improved – Redesigned the Setup Wizard with a step sidebar, a fixed footer and steps styled to match the admin panel.
  • Improved – Redesigned the Dashboard’s Pro banner, the notifications dropdown, the Group settings page, the menu-item role restriction dialog and the right sidebar’s Trending posts and Recent activities widgets.
  • Improved – Hover animations on the community’s top navigation, left sidebar, feed view toggles, sidebar widgets and admin tabs and filters.
  • Improved – Pro features (Pro post types, settings tabs, add-ons) stay visible with a PRO tag when Pro is inactive, and clicking a PRO tag opens the upgrade dialog.
  • Improved – Attachment upload limits now follow your server’s maximum upload size instead of a fixed 20MB.
  • Improved – Images in ticket conversations sit side by side, and an image sent without text no longer shows its file name as the message.
  • Improved – Post cards have tighter spacing between the header, text and media.
  • Fixed – A site administrator could get a 401 and lose access to their own community after choosing “Only selected roles can view” in the Setup Wizard, before adding their own role to the allow-list; admins now always bypass this check, the same way they already do for member-visibility.
  • Fixed – A SCORM-packaged course (Academy LMS v4.0.0’s SCORM addon) showed no lesson count or duration on its course card, since a SCORM course intentionally has an empty lesson list; it now shows a “SCORM course” label there instead.
  • Fixed – Writing a private note on a member’s ticket-sidebar profile could lose the note or clear the box unexpectedly; adding a note is now a proper save action with its own button, and a failed save keeps your draft instead of discarding it.
  • Fixed – The post composer, anonymous post form, and post edit form could each attach the same uploaded image twice.
  • Fixed – A dropdown built with react-select (used throughout Settings, including attaching a crawl result to a knowledge base) rendered a few pixels taller than the button or input sitting beside it. WP-admin’s own field styling was reaching inside react-select’s hidden typeahead input and inflating it; the control is now pinned to the same height as its neighboring inputs and buttons.
  • Fixed – The Agent Activity page’s Activity/Knowledge Gaps tab strip had no divider line under the inactive tab, only under the active one, from an invalid kebab-cased style prop that was silently ignored.
  • Fixed – Anonymous posts only list Spaces that allow anonymous posting, with a clearer message when none do; the post type is now chosen before the Space.
  • Fixed – Opening a group from a collection in the left sidebar no longer collapses that collection; the collection now stays open and is highlighted.
  • Fixed – The Setup Wizard page printed a PHP “print_emoji_styles is deprecated” notice before loading.
  • Fixed – Several admin console errors, including missing imports, an unregistered editor table module and settings tabs mounting while their add-on was off.
  • Fixed – Dropdown menus (e.g. Collection on the Group settings page) were cut off by the section border, and table action tooltips were clipped on the first row.

2.2.0 – 03/09/2026

  • Changed – The AI agent’s name now defaults to “Ava” and is said out loud: the assistant opens a conversation with “Hi, I’m Ava, the virtual assistant for “. The name field on Settings -> AI Agent says where the name is used, and the description field beside it – collected since the addon shipped and read by nothing – is now the “what your business does” line the assistant answers from.
  • Fixed – Settings -> Live chat told every site to install the Live Chat plugin on the site it was connecting, on every visit, directly above the table listing the sites that had already done it. The instructions now appear only while nothing is connected; the download stays on the heading.
  • Improved – The community asks the server far less to open a page. Identical requests that are already in flight are shared rather than repeated, so the three notification calls that used to fire in the same millisecond are one; ticket counters follow the statuses and assignments they are derived from instead of refetching on every poll; and the six small things every page needs — settings, menus, the welcome banner, sidebar widgets, group permissions and the group tree — arrive together from a single /bootstrap request instead of six that each pay WordPress’s startup cost. Measured on the community home: fourteen requests and 99 KB down to six and 36 KB.
  • Improved – Menu icons are sent once each rather than repeated inline for every item in every menu, which took the menus response from 38 KB to 24 KB on every page load.
  • Improved – The member directory is no longer loaded on every page in the community. The two screens that read it — mentions, and the “closed by” name on a ticket — ask for it themselves.
  • Fixed – A member with no avatar caused a request to a hostname built by string concatenation (“example.comnull”), so every such page spent a DNS lookup failing to resolve it. Seven places that built media URLs this way now share one helper that cannot.
  • Fixed – The profile avatar built its URL with a trailing space inside it.
  • Accessibility – The app shell declares the site’s language, exposes its content as a main landmark, and the logo has an accessible name.

2.1.0 – 31/08/2026

  • Added – Date of Birth field (opt-in, off by default) and minor-safe messaging: when enabled, adults can no longer start a private message or send into a group chat with a member flagged as a minor, while a minor can still reach an adult; the check fails open for anyone with no Date of Birth on file, so turning the setting on never retroactively blocks existing conversations.
  • Added – Upvote/downvote voting via a new “Idea” post type: a dedicated composer tab posts vote-only content (regular posts keep the existing Like button), with a pro-gated “Top Ideas” sort.
  • Added – “Team Post” composer tab (Pro, group admins/moderators) to post under the group’s identity, and a dedicated “Allow Anonymous Comments” group setting (separate from the existing anonymous-post setting, Pro), plus a clearer, more visible anonymous-comment toggle in the composer that only appears when the group allows it.
  • Added – Member moderation actions for groups: warn, mute, and a timed auto-expiring suspend, alongside the existing permanent ban.
  • Added – Group “first post requires approval” setting so a new member’s first post can be held for admin review before it’s visible.
  • Added – Group rules, with a rich-text info box editor for admins to explain them.
  • Added – A real, editable title field in the post composer instead of always auto-generating it from the post body.
  • Added – A dark-mode site logo option, shown automatically when the theme is in dark mode.
  • Fixed – Select dropdown text was unreadable in dark mode.
  • Added – Auto-saved ticket drafts, editor keyboard shortcuts, Cmd/Ctrl+K link paste, and general UI polish in the ticket composer.
  • Added – Support for a message/variable in the ticket auto-close notice.
  • Added – Notification links now go directly to the related post/feed instead of a generic page.
  • Added – A “Remove logo” button in the branding settings.
  • Added – “About” and “Connection” (the renamed, merged Follower/Following tabs) are now managed from Menu Settings → Profile Menu instead of being hardcoded, alongside a new “Bookmarked” entry, and all three can be reordered like any other menu item.
  • Added – Accy7ount & Profile: custom display name and pronouns (shown on the profile header, in mention hover cards, and search), the community avatar now syncs to the site-wide WordPress avatar, a profile-completion progress bar, per-user follow-list privacy with a merged “Connections” (Followers/Following) tab, and automatic badge assignment based on admin-defined rules (role, group membership, points, or a profile field being filled in).
  • Added – Notification emails now include a magic-link “View in Community” button that signs the recipient in on click, plus a per-user email delivery preference (send right away, or batch into a daily/weekly digest).
  • Improved – Raised the “Read more” truncation length for posts (250 → 600 characters) and comments (160 → 320 characters) so normal-length content no longer gets cut short.
  • Fixed – A group’s tab list could reorder or fold the Discussion and Featured tabs into the customizable tab set; they’re now always two fixed, separate tabs regardless of custom tab ordering.
  • Fixed – Group names now truncate with an ellipsis (with a tooltip showing the full name) instead of hard-cutting or wrapping across lines, consistently across post cards, the schedule view, single post view, group header, grid/list views, the sidebar, and the admin Users table.
  • Fixed – Posts and comments now render paragraph/list/blockquote spacing correctly instead of collapsing into unstyled raw text.
  • Fixed – The Follow/Unfollow button on a post card’s hover mini-profile rendered as an invisible white-on-white box in dark mode.
  • Fixed – Clicking a reaction emoji left the reaction tray open instead of closing it, most noticeable on touch devices.
  • Added – A confirmation prompt before losing an in-progress post, comment, ticket, or chat message you’ve started typing — covers the post composer, comment box, new-ticket drawer, ticket replies, direct/group messages, and the floating chat bubble, plus a browser warning if you close or reload the tab with unsent text.
  • Fixed – Selecting a group while composing a post could trigger an unwanted zoom-in on mobile Safari that required a pinch gesture to undo.
  • Fixed – The notifications dropdown could extend past the edge of the screen on mobile, requiring horizontal scrolling to see the full panel.
  • Fixed – The AI agent could stop responding on a ticket after its first reply and never resume; a background job that silently failed to start is now automatically retried within a few minutes instead of being lost.
  • Fixed – Ticket activity notes (e.g. “assigned to…”) were unreadable in dark mode.
  • Fixed – Ticket ID numbers (“#1”, “#2″…) in the admin ticket list were nearly invisible in dark mode.

2.0.1 – 12/08/2026

short_description: All-in-one WordPress community plugin: groups, posts, real-time chat, support tickets & live chat.
description:
The All-in-One WordPress Community Plugin for Groups, Social Feeds, Real-Time Chat, and Support

ZenCommunity is the first WordPress community plugin that unifies groups, posts, support ticketing, and live chat into one native powerhouse. Build social, Facebook-style communities with real-time chat and posts, convert community posts into tracked support tickets, and offer instant live help — all inside your WordPress site.

👉 ZenCommunity Site
👉 Unlock Premium Features
👉 Join Our Official Community

Core Features at a Glance

Community Tool

  • User-friendly UX
  • Unlimited groups/spaces
  • User profiles
  • Activity feeds
  • Member controls
  • Feeds
  • Comments & reactions
  • Real-time chat
  • Notifications
  • Privacy controls
  • Mentions
  • Hashtags
  • Polls and surveys (Coming soon)
  • Leaderboard (Coming soon)
  • Bookmarks
  • Branding options
  • Welcome message
  • Custom slugs
  • Search
  • Member directory
  • File uploads
  • GIF
  • Emoji
  • Media storage
  • Role manager
  • User approval
  • Email summaries
  • Dark & light mode

Support Ticketing [PRO]

  • Convert feed to tickets
  • Ticket status tracking
  • Ticket assignment
  • Ticket stages (ongoing, solved, etc.)
  • Ticket notifications
  • Auto replies (Coming soon)

Live Chat [PRO]

  • Customizable website live chat widget (Cross domain also supported)
  • Multi-session handling
  • Instant visitor support
  • Real-time notifications
  • File sharing
  • 24/7 support system

ZenCommunity isn’t just another community plugin. It’s the first WordPress solution that combines the three strongest engagement systems — Community, Real-Time Chat, and Support Tickets — together in one place.

Most WordPress websites use 3–5 different tools to achieve what ZenCommunity does alone. That creates scattered conversations, missed messages, and poor user experience. ZenCommunity removes that problem completely.

By keeping community posts, chats, and support inside one system, your users stay connected, engaged, and supported without ever leaving your site.
Below are the core sections that show how ZenCommunity stands out.

Community Features — Your Full Social System Inside WordPress

ZenCommunity gives you everything needed to build a full, social-style community inside WordPress — no third-party platforms, no separate plugins.

Advanced Community Groups

Build public or private groups with full admin control. Groups can be used for LMS classes, client spaces, internal teams, membership circles, or interest-based communities. Each group has its own feed, members, and settings.

Facebook-Style Posting & Engagement

Your members can publish posts, attach media, use @mentions, comment, reply, react, and follow discussions. The interface feels familiar, simple, and fast — encouraging users to talk and stay active.

Real-Time Community Chat

ZenCommunity includes built-in chat inside groups. Members can start private one-to-one chats or chat as a group with typing indicators, read status, file sharing, and notifications. Conversations stay active without page reloads.

User Profiles & Activity Tracking

Each user gets a profile with activity, groups, posts, and engagement. This makes your community feel more personal and interactive.

Community Growth Features

Hashtags, polls, surveys, leaderboards, bookmarks, and email summaries help keep engagement high. Members always have a reason to come back.

Admin Control & Community Safety

Moderators can manage posts, approve members, customize branding, set privacy rules, and control roles. You decide how open or private each group should be.

Support Ticketing — Full Helpdesk Inside Your Community

ZenCommunity includes a complete support ticketing system connected directly to your community and chats.

Convert Posts Into Support Tickets

If a user posts a question that needs deeper help, convert it into a ticket with one click — no platform switching.

Clear Ticket Assignments

Assign each ticket to a responsible team member so the right person handles the issue. This reduces confusion and improves response time.

Status Tracking

Each ticket has clear stages (new, ongoing, solved, etc.) so both sides can follow progress. Your support team stays organized, and users always know what’s happening.

Personal Support Chat on Each Ticket

Tickets include an instant one-to-one chat. Users don’t need email or external help desks — everything is live and inside your site.

Smart Notifications

Both users and team members get notifications when ticket updates happen. Nothing gets lost.

Auto Replies

Helpful for off-hours, acknowledgment messages, or routing requests.

Live Chat — Instant Help That Converts Visitors

ZenCommunity includes a built-in real-time live chat widget for your entire site.

Customizable Widget

Add your supporter’s name, photo, availability status, and greeting message. This makes your support feel personal and trustworthy.

Instant Visitor Support

Visitors can start chatting immediately. Control visitor login or anonymous chat.

Multi-Session Handling

Support agents can handle multiple conversations at once without losing track.

Real-Time Notifications & File Sharing

Send and receive files instantly, get notified when new messages arrive, and keep the conversation going smoothly.

24/7 Support System

The widget stays active at all times, so users always have access to help.

Who ZenCommunity Helps

ZenCommunity fits a wide range of websites and business types:

  • LMS websites (students + instructors)
  • Membership sites
  • Local groups & communities
  • Agencies
  • SaaS companies
  • E-commerce stores
  • Service providers
  • Creators & educators
  • Internal teams & organizations

🔥 Deep Academy LMS Integration

ZenCommunity connects directly with Academy LMS to automate all your course activities inside your community — without any extra work from the admin.
When this integration is enabled, key Academy LMS events automatically create posts in your ZenCommunity groups. This means your learners stay updated, active, and informed without any manual posting.

What Automatically Gets Shared

ZenCommunity can post updates in your community when any of the following events happen inside Academy LMS:

  • Course Enrolled
  • Course Complete
  • Course Announcements
  • User Question
  • Question Answer
  • Lesson Update
  • Quiz Start
  • Quiz End

This makes ZenCommunity the perfect LMS community plugin.

Extended LMS Integrations

ZenCommunity now supports multiple popular WordPress LMS plugins, making it easy to add community, discussion, chat, and support features to your learning website.

Tutor LMS Integration with ZenCommunity

ZenCommunity integrates with Tutor LMS to bring key course activities directly into your community groups, helping learners stay informed and engaged inside WordPress.

This integration turns Tutor LMS course progress into visible community updates, encouraging discussion around learning milestones.

Tutor LMS Events Shared in ZenCommunity

When Tutor LMS integration is enabled, the following course activities are automatically posted in ZenCommunity group feeds:

  • Course Enrollment
  • Topic Complete
  • Course Complete
  • Quiz Start
  • Quiz End

Each event appears inside the selected community group, allowing students and instructors to interact around real course progress in real time.

LearnPress Integration with ZenCommunity

ZenCommunity integrates with LearnPress to connect course activity, learner questions, and progress updates directly with your community groups.

This integration helps LearnPress users turn learning actions into shared discussions, keeping students active and connected inside WordPress.

LearnPress Events Shared in ZenCommunity

When LearnPress integration is enabled, the following course activities are automatically posted in ZenCommunity group feeds:

  • Course Enrollment
  • Course Complete
  • Lesson Completion
  • User Question
  • Question Answer
  • Quiz Start
  • Quiz End

These updates appear inside the selected community groups, allowing learners and instructors to interact around real learning progress in one place.

MasterStudy LMS Integration with ZenCommunity

ZenCommunity integrates with MasterStudy LMS to connect course progress, learner questions, and completion updates directly with your community groups.

This integration helps MasterStudy-based learning sites turn course activity into shared discussions, keeping learners engaged inside WordPress.

MasterStudy LMS Events Shared in ZenCommunity

When MasterStudy LMS integration is enabled, the following course activities are automatically posted in ZenCommunity group feeds:

  • Course Enrollment
  • Course Complete
  • Lesson Completion
  • User Question
  • Question Answer
  • Quiz End

These updates appear inside the selected community groups, allowing students and instructors to interact around real learning progress in one place.

Lifter LMS Integration with ZenCommunity

ZenCommunity integrates with Lifter LMS to bring course activity, learner questions, and progress updates directly into your community groups.

This integration helps Lifter LMS websites keep students engaged through shared discussions and real-time updates inside WordPress.

Lifter LMS Events Shared in ZenCommunity

When Lifter LMS integration is enabled, the following course activities are automatically posted in ZenCommunity group feeds:

  • Course Enrollment
  • Course Complete
  • Lesson Completion
  • User Question
  • Question Answer
  • Quiz End

These updates appear inside the selected community groups, allowing learners and instructors to interact around real course progress in one central place.

LearnDash Integration with ZenCommunity

LearnDash integrates with ZenCommunity to connect course activity directly with your community groups, helping learners stay active and engaged inside WordPress.

This integration turns LearnDash progress into shared community updates, encouraging discussion, motivation, and peer interaction around learning milestones.

LearnDash Events Shared in ZenCommunity

When LearnDash integration is enabled, the following course activities are automatically posted in ZenCommunity group feeds:

  • Course Enrollment
  • Course Complete
  • Topic Complete
  • Quiz End

Each event appears inside the selected community group, allowing students and instructors to interact around real course progress in real time.

This makes ZenCommunity a strong companion for LearnDash-based learning sites that want to combine structured courses with active community engagement.

⚡ Performance & Reliability

  • ZenCommunity is built for speed:
  • No external tools
  • No outside servers
  • No extra apps
  • Everything loads inside WordPress
  • Real-time updates with lightweight scripts
    The plugin is optimized for both small sites and enterprise-level communities.

🛠 Admin Tools

Site admins get:

  • A single dashboard for groups, posts, tickets, and chats
  • Role-based permissions
  • Community moderation controls
  • Branding settings
  • Full visibility into engagement and support activity

Source Code

The compiled JavaScript and CSS in assets/build/ are generated from human-readable sources kept in the public repository:

https://github.com/kodezen/zencommunity

  • JavaScript/React sources: dev_zencommunity/ (admin app in dev_zencommunity/Admin/, block editor integration in dev_zencommunity/fse/)
  • Build configuration: package.json, webpack.config.js, tailwind.config.js, tailwind.admin.config.js, postcss.config.js
  • PHP dependencies: composer.json

To build the assets yourself:

  1. Clone the repository and install Node.js 20 or later and Composer.
  2. Run npm ci --legacy-peer-deps, then npm run build (compiles everything into assets/build/).
  3. Run composer install to install the PHP dependencies.

External services

ZenCommunity works entirely on your own site. It contacts an external service only in the cases below.

Kodezen usage insights and deactivation feedback (store.kodezen.com)

ZenCommunity uses the StoreEngine SDK to talk to Kodezen’s store at https://store.kodezen.com/.

  • Usage insights (opt-in only). After installation, an admin notice asks whether you want to share usage data. Nothing is sent unless an administrator clicks “Allow”. If you allow it, the plugin sends: site URL and name, admin name and email, server IP address, operating system, WordPress/PHP/MySQL and server versions, PHP settings and extensions, locale, multisite status, the active theme, active and inactive plugins, and the plugin version. After that it reports the same data about once a week. You can opt out at any time under ZenCommunity → Settings → License.
  • Deactivation feedback. When you deactivate the plugin, an optional form asks why and lists what will be sent. Only if you click “Submit & Deactivate” does it send the reason, any comment you type, your name and email, the site name and URL, and the usage data listed above. Choosing “Skip & Deactivate” sends nothing.

This service is provided by Kodezen: Terms of Use, Privacy Policy.

Link previews (the websites members link to)

When a logged-in member hovers over a link in a post or comment, your site fetches that link’s page once to show its title, description and image in a preview card. The request goes from your server to the linked website, and sends only the page address and a user agent that names your site. Nothing about the member is sent. For video and media links (for example YouTube or Vimeo) the details come from that service’s public oEmbed endpoint, from the list of providers built into WordPress, instead of the page itself. Results are cached for a day. The preview image is then loaded by the member’s browser from the linked website. Nothing is fetched until someone hovers over a link, and logged-out visitors see only the address. Developers can turn this off with add_filter( 'zencommunity/link_preview/enabled', '__return_false' );. Each linked website’s own terms and privacy policy apply.

Links to other Kodezen products

The “Extend your Community” dashboard section and the Live Chat settings link to product pages and downloads on https://store.kodezen.com/. These are plain links that open in your browser, and no data is sent until you click one. Products hosted on WordPress.org (for example GameEngine, GemBooking and Zaplane) are installed only when an administrator clicks “Install”. They come from WordPress.org through WordPress’s own plugin installer.
